review_scope: Source test setup, assertions and called C++ fixture contracts; not full implementing-leaf acceptance
review_notes: New fixture_select declares meaningful comment/purpose in trusted test code. Public query, nested relation and aggregate inputs now use it; C++ fixtures already bind explicit intent.
Mutation and ledger fixtures explicitly bind MutationIntent or root comments. Existing direct C++ fixtures use actual runtime intent constructors and governed private entry points.

The memory aggregate struct literal initializes new facets, relation_aggregates, purpose, readonly definitions and dynamic selection fields to empty/None. This cfg(test)-only helper remains reference-only, separate from the public in-memory engine.
One entity-binding assertion now constructs fixture_select(repo.entity()) instead of repo.select(); expected entity remains Order. The C++ counterpart retains its entity/select binding assertions.

Other business assertions, expected rows, counts, errors, checker paths, relation keys, ordering, cache/TTL/principal and lock behavior remain the historical reviewed contracts. Direct source and C++ execution supply current evidence rather than a baseline-label update.

Production root adds commit_audit, document_round_trip, dynamic_fields, shared metadata decoder and DynamicFieldChanges declarations/reexports. Root-test execution does not qualify every implementing leaf or generated configuration.
